title: Speed up a count of ways
prompt: A staircase has n steps. You climb one or two steps at a time. Return the number of different ways to reach the top. There is one way to climb 0 steps. The starter is correct, but for 60 steps it would run for years, so the last check reports a time limit. Rewrite it so that each smaller answer is worked out once.
hints: How many times does the starter work out the answer for 3 steps while answering for 6?
Store each answer the first time it is worked out, in a Map or an array.
Fill an array from the bottom: ways[0] = 1, ways[1] = 1, and ways[i] = ways[i - 1] + ways[i - 2] up to n.
checkLabels: One step can be climbed in 1 way.
Two steps can be climbed in 2 ways.
Five steps can be climbed in 8 ways.
There is one way to climb no steps.
Sixty steps must be answered within the time limit.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Works out the same smaller answers again and again, so a large input never finishes.
Starts the table one place off, so every answer belongs to the staircase one step shorter.

feedback: The recursion is right. What it lacks is memory: every smaller staircase should be answered once and then looked up.
